events.title: Leo III is elected pope
events.description: Leo III was elected pope, becoming bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States until his death in 816. On Christmas Day 800 he crowned Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica.
events.html: Leo III was elected pope, becoming bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States until his death in 816. On Christmas Day 800 he crowned Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica.

events.title: Shakespeare's King Lear is performed before King James I
events.description: William Shakespeare's tragedy King Lear, based on the legend of Leir of Britain, was performed before King James I, the earliest performance on record, noted in the Stationers' Register. The play was probably written in late 1605 or early 1606.

events.title: Handel's opera Agrippina premieres in Venice
events.description: George Frideric Handel's opera Agrippina, described as his first masterpiece, had its premiere in Venice. Its libretto by Cardinal Vincenzo Grimani followed Agrippina, mother of Nero, as she plotted the downfall of the emperor Claudius.

events.title: Washington defeats the Hessians at Trenton
events.description: Washington's army surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton, capturing about 900 soldiers with few American losses. The victory revived the Revolution after months of defeat.
events.html: Washington's army surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton, capturing about 900 soldiers with few American losses. The victory revived the Revolution after months of defeat.

events.title: Louis XVI assents to the Civil Constitution of the Clergy
events.description: Having first opposed it, King Louis XVI gave his public assent to the Civil Constitution of the Clergy, which sought state control of the Catholic Church in France. The clergy's oaths followed, and the resulting schism lasted until 1801.

events.title: The Decembrist revolt fails in St Petersburg
events.description: Army officers led troops onto Senate Square to refuse allegiance to Nicholas I and demand reform. Cannon fire dispersed them; five leaders were hanged, and the Decembrists inspired later Russian radicals.
events.html: Army officers led troops onto Senate Square to refuse allegiance to Nicholas I and demand reform. Cannon fire dispersed them; five leaders were hanged, and the Decembrists inspired later Russian radicals.

events.title: The Curies announce the discovery of radium
events.description: A paper presented to the French Academy of Sciences announced radium, a new element found in pitchblende by Marie and Pierre Curie with Gustave Bémont. It later proved vital in early cancer treatment.

events.title: An earthquake and tsunami devastate the Indian Ocean
events.description: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra sent tsunamis across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in 14 countries. Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand were worst hit.
